newsitem.title: USA: Sun Health to sell outpatient rehab clinics.
newsitem.headline: Sun Health to sell outpatient rehab clinics.

text.p: Sun Healthcare Group Inc said Thursday it plans to sell and divest its outpatient rehabilitation therapy clinics in the United States, as well as Columbia Health Care Inc, its Canadian outpatient rehabilitation therapy unit.
Sun Healthcare said it decided to sell the facilities since the operations were "not sufficiently synergistic with either the company's inpatient or ancillary service businesses."

The expected sale of the operations is expected to occur at or near their book value for no material gain or loss. The sales, however, will have a slightly positive impact on future results of operations. The company did not elaborate.
Sun Healthcare said it acquired the U.S. clinics as part of the company's acquisition of Mediplex. The Columbia clinics in Canada were purchased in separate transactions in 1995.
The sale of both operations is expected to be completed by year-end 1997.
Separately, Sun Healthcare posted first quarter earnings of $0.33 per fully diluted share, compared with $0.31 per fully diluted share a year ago.
